newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk far right party withdraws coalition support.
newsitem.headline: Turk far right party withdraws coalition support.

text.p: A Turkish far right party said on Thursday it was withdrawing its support from the Islamist-led coalition government, cutting its majority in parliament to a handful of votes.
The announcement was made by Grand Unity Party (BBP) leader Muhsin Yazicioglu, whose party has seven deputies in the 550-member assembly.
"We are withdrawing the support which we have given to this government as of this moment," Yazicioglu said at a news conference.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party and its alliance partner, the conservative True Path Party (DYP), have a total of 279 parliamentary seats.
The coalition was established last June and shortly afterwards won a confidence vote in parliament with the support of the BBP.

Concern in the alliance that some members of Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller's DYP would oppose the unlikely coalition was expected to give the BBP deputies a key role in the vote's outcome, but ultimately their support was unnecessary.
Yazicioglu cited "injustice" in the running of government as a reason for the decision. A report in the Islamist daily Zaman said the BBP was planning to withdraw support over unjust wage increases.
